newsitem.title: USA: US WCoast prods firm with NYMEX, Bay stays firm.
newsitem.headline: US WCoast prods firm with NYMEX, Bay stays firm.

text.p: U.S. West Coast products prices edged up early with futures, but Los Angeles distillates stayed weak relative to the Bay area, prompted by supply fears.
Traders reported a unspecified problem at Shell's Martinez, Calif., refinery.
But a company spokeswoman denied the rumor.
"There's been no problems that I'm aware of," she said.
Offers for low sulphur diesel in San Francisco rose a half cent to 72.50 cents a gallon.
Los Angeles offers rose in tandem, but remained one cent cheaper after falling below the Bay late last week amid talk of refinery problems.
L.A. low sulphur bids stayed unchanged at 70 cents a gallon.
Jet fuel in the Bay rose one cent to 71/72 cents, with the Bay a cent higher.
Rumors circulated of a problem with a fluid catalytic cracking unit at Ultramar's Wilmington, Calif. refinery, which processes roughly 70,000 barrels per day of crude oil.
The company was not immediately available to comment.

Gasolines prices turned mixed, with CARB regular in Los Angeles down a half cent for offers at 72.50 cents a gallon, while conventional rose a cent, in line with an 0.94 cent-rise in NYMEX unleaded gasoline for November delivery.
NYMEX unleaded traded 63.20 in late New York discussion.
